note: Expected verdicts are the dataset author's judgement, not a faculty consensus. Where reasonable reviewers could differ, `accept` lists every verdict that is defensible and `ambiguous` is true; those items are left out of the false-positive and false-negative rates. A faculty panel should review, correct and extend this file before any threshold is set from it.

reviewProcess: Faculty: for each item read source, target and the expected verdict(s); enter your own verdict in facultyVerdict (ALIGNED, PARTIALLY_ALIGNED or NOT_ALIGNED) and a note. Where reasonable reviewers disagree, record that in facultyNotes rather than forcing one answer. Set reviewStatus to "faculty-reviewed" per item only after review; set the dataset reviewStatus to "faculty-reviewed" only when every item has been.

changeLog.change: Metadata only: reviewStatus, facultyVerdict, facultyNotes and diagnosis fields added; the course/disciplines gaps are listed in `gaps`. NO expected verdict was changed, so results remain comparable with eval-1.

gaps: Calculus is 25 of 41 items; nursing is 4. ILO-content, Module-value, Description-plan, REF-plan and CLO-anyPO are tested in calculus only.
CLO-EGA has 2 items and no clear-ALIGNED example; CLO-anyPO has 2; REF-plan has 3. Per-type rates for these are not meaningful yet.
Only 13 items are clear-ALIGNED against 21 clear not-aligned, so the false-positive rate rests on little data.
No INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE example (empty or unreadable text), no Filipino/Tagalog text, no year-3/4 course, no education, business or humanities course.
Every item is a single isolated pair; the real checker sends up to 12 mixed pairs per call, and results can differ between a pair asked alone and in a batch (seen for ILO-CLO and REF-plan).
No example of a CLO tagged to several POs or an ILO tagged to several CLOs (that policy lives in engine.js and is covered by engine tests, not by this dataset).
